More pieces here than most comps, but no named or better patterns seen, so likely $30 to $70 hammer.

lots.working: Same-item class taken as Gowans multi-piece marigold box lots of about 6 to 10 pieces sold in the last 24 months: $65, $45, $42, $35, $20. Keep: lowest $20 / 1.22 = $16.39, round down to $15. Flip: likely resale = median of those five = $42 hammer; less an assumed 20% vendor commission at a Tasmanian room = $33.60; no outbound postage (bulky glass, resold locally at auction); $33.60 / 2.44 = $13.77, round down to $10. Buyer is local, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification as common marigold carnival and many opened Gowans SOLD records that agree, but no maker's mark read and rims and bases not shown close up, so High is not met.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: Gowans 386369 (QTY OF CARNIVAL & AMBER GLASS, $60), 365494 (coloured glassware incl. one carnival piece, $70) and 392404 (amber platter and 4 carnival items, $90): mixed lots where the carnival share of the price cannot be separated. Gowans 408112 (Kookaburra bowl, $55) and 392312 (Magpie master bowl set, $80): named Australian bird patterns, a different and better item than anything in lot 452. Underpriced AI aggregator page (USD 25 median of 41 eBay sales): a statistic, not a single verifiable sale, and its listed comps include unrelated pieces (a Jeannette spittoon, a Northwood creamer); category context only. All Gowans records were re-fetched and title, sale_price, bid_count and auction id matched the researcher's claims; photos for the close entries were checked on a contact sheet.
lots.key_photo_findings: Three photos confirm 12 pieces, all marigold. Large fruit bowl has arched panels with diamond lattice; feather or peacock-tail style ruffled bowl, a rose-type ruffled bowl and a ribbed round bowl are clearly seen. Two mugs and the tall vase have gilt rims and a marigold-to-clear fade, typical of later pressed iridescent ware. No bases, marks or close rim views. Iridescence looks even and fairly bright; no obvious chips at photo resolution.
lots.condition: No damage visible in the photos, but rims and bases are not shown close up and wear to the lustre cannot be judged.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are there any chips, flea bites or cracks to the rims or feet, and are any maker's marks (for example a Crown Crystal or Fenton mark) on the bases? Is the lot exactly the 12 pieces photographed?

lots.what_it_is: Four pieces: (1) Wade Heath England honey-glazed trough planter moulded with tulips and green leaves, black WADE HEATH ENGLAND stamp read on the base (1930s to 1940s style mark); (2) dark blue jasper-dip style biscuit barrel with white sprigged classical figure and putti, plated rim, lid and swing handle, maker not seen; (3) cream salt-glaze stein with a blue crown over HB (Hofbrauhaus Munchen style) and a pewter lid, probably a later souvenir; (4) green glazed bell-shaped pierced posy holder moulded 'DIGUE DIN DON' round the shoulder (French style), maker not seen.
lots.score_reason: The Wade Heath trough is the best piece but no sale of it was found; the nearest Wade planters made about $32 each at Gowans. Unmarked plated jasper barrels and souvenir steins sell for about $10 to $25 each in Tasmania. As a group likely $40 to $80 hammer.

Range $20 to $50 AUD, all SOLD, none UNSOLD or ASKING. lots.working: No SOLD result for the same item (this four-piece group, or the Wade Heath tulip trough itself) was found, and the two close entries are group lots for single components, so no maximum bid can be set on the rules. Indicative only: Wade planter about $32 + barrel share about $15 + stein about $10 + posy about $5 = roughly $60 hammer, not a bid limit.
lots.confidence_reason: Wade Heath mark is clearly read, but there is no SOLD evidence for the trough and the barrel's maker is unconfirmed, so value rests on component and category guides.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. All 11 Gowans records were re-fetched: titles, sale_price, bid_count and auction ids matched the researcher; photos for the close entries (373585, 411911) and the Wade comp (367327) were checked and match the descriptions. One WebSearch for Wade Heath tulip trough sales returned only an eBay listing (closed to us, snippet only, sale status unknown), not used.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3 clearly shows the black hand-stamped WADE HEATH ENGLAND mark with fine crazing and three kiln pad marks. Photo 2 shows the trough sound with crisp moulding. The barrel shows a sprigged standing female figure between two winged putti, plated lid with finial and swing handle; its base is not photographed so no Wedgwood or Adams mark is visible. Enlarged crop of the bell reads 'DIGUE DIN DON' repeated round the shoulder, pierced top for stems. Stein has a crown over HB in blue and a pewter lid with thumb-piece.
lots.condition: No chips or cracks visible on the trough apart from crazing typical of the age. Other pieces look sound at photo resolution; plated mounts on the barrel look lightly worn; stein lid hinge and barrel base not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is there a maker's mark on the base of the blue biscuit barrel (Wedgwood, Adams or other), and is the jasper solid or dipped? Any chips, cracks or restoration on the Wade Heath trough rim? Is the stein's pewter lid hinge intact, and is there any mark on the green bell posy holder?

lots.what_it_is: Mixed box of glass and ceramics, nothing marked or signed in the photos. Best pieces: four cobalt blue glass bowls (one larger, three smaller) with a wide gilt grape-vine band (Bohemian style, probably mid 20th century), a blue and white cased handkerchief (fazzoletto) style vase with multicolour streaks, an amber crackle glass pedestal bowl with a vase insert, and a blue glass flower on a green block. The rest is minor: two moulded pottery souvenir steins, a gilt-rimmed transfer-printed tankard and mug, a ceramic toast rack, a Chinese calligraphy table screen, a red resin desk stand, a stone trinket box, an amber glass ashtray and a quartz clock and weather desk set.
lots.score_reason: A typical mixed box with two or three decorative glass pieces. Similar mixed glass and china boxes at Gowans made $15 to $110, mostly $30 to $60. Nothing marked, so probably $40 to $80 hammer.

lots.guide_summary: No same-item or close entry survives: the two entries the researcher called close (an amber Bohemian dessert set and a pair of Tango vases) are different items and were downgraded to category guides. All remaining evidence is SOLD category guides at Gowans: mixed glass and china boxes $15 to $110 (mostly $30 to $60), cobalt gilt glass lots $20 to $55, single art glass vases $30 to $110. No UNSOLD or ASKING evidence. All AUD, rate 1.00.
lots.working: No SOLD result for the same item or a close match, so no maximum bid on the rules. Category guide only: similar mixed boxes at Gowans cluster at $30 to $60 hammer.
lots.confidence_reason: Nothing marked or signed, maker and age of the glass unconfirmed, and value rests on category guides only.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: Gowans 400082 (QTY OF GLASS FLOWERS, $120): about ten long-stem glass flowers, a quantity lot not comparable to one flower on a block. Gowans 438315 and 424788 (boxes of German steins, $76 and $50): German stoneware steins in bulk, not comparable to the box's two moulded pottery souvenir steins. Reclassified: 413525 and 431140 moved from close to category guide (different items). All other Gowans records were re-fetched and title, sale_price, bid_count and auction id matched the researcher.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2 shows the four cobalt bowls clearly: wide gilt band with grape vines between narrow gilt lines, three smaller bowls on short feet, gilt looks bright with no obvious wear. The vase is cased white inside with blue outside and multicolour streaks, ruffled rim. Amber piece is crackle glass with applied prunts and a vase insert. Steins are moulded brown pottery with tavern scenes, not lustre. Clock is a three-dial clock, thermometer and hygrometer desk piece. No marks or bases shown on any piece.
lots.condition: No damage visible, but rims and bases are not shown close up; gilt on the cobalt bowls looks largely intact.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are there any chips to the rims of the cobalt gilt bowls or the handkerchief vase, and any wear to the gilt? Are there any labels or marks (for example Bohemia or Murano stickers) on the glass?
